Title: Anew

Title: Christ Church Cathedral
Description: Step into | Christ Church Cathedral, | and it’s like stepping into Dublin’s secret medieval time capsule, it’s nearly a thousand years old and was originally a Viking church built around AD 1030. As you wander through awe‑inspiring Gothic arches and whispery stone halls, kids will love spotting the mummified cat and rat tucked away in the crypt—because what’s more memorable than museum-level rodents stuck in eternity? You can also see the tomb of the famous Strongbow and (gulp!) the heart of Saint Laurence O’Toole. Talk about tangible history that’s equal parts fascinating and face‑palm funny. | But wait, it gets better. Families can | totally | get hands‑on here: don a medieval knight’s tunic or Tudor hat in the crypt’s dress‑up corner, relive the tale of Strongbow and Aoife, or even play at being an 18th-century stallholder. And if any brave child is aged 12 or over? They—and even grown‑ups—can clamber up to the belfry and try their hand at ringing Christ Church’s famous bells. It’s not just an indoor activity—it’s a full-on, historic, hands-on adventure that’ll have little ones buzzing with stories for days! | With combo‑ticket options that include | Dublinia | next door, it’s the perfect indoor family day out—historic, hands-on, and hilariously educational.

Title: Collins Barracks
Description: FREE ADMISSION | Collins Barracks, | now home to the National Museum of Ireland’s | Decorative Arts & History, | is a treasure trove of culture, creativity, and, best of all, absolutely free fun. The galleries are bursting with fascinating exhibits, from military history to fashion, art, and design, making it a perfect stop for curious kids and grown-ups alike. And because admission won’t cost a cent, it’s the ideal place to pop into on a rainy Dublin day. | What makes Collins Barracks extra special, though, is its lineup of | brilliant free events | . Families can dive into hands-on days like “Game On! A Day of Play”, where little ones get stuck into giant games, crafty challenges, and playful themed tours. The museum also runs Heritage Week activities, including tours that explore everything from vintage fashion in “The Way We Wore” to music, sport, and even LGBTQIA+ history. Add in Culture Night celebrations, quirky workshops like the Dead Zoo Lab, and the ever-popular free lunchtime concerts by The Army No. 1 Band, and you’ve got a spot that’s just as entertaining as it is educational. | Discover a wild side of Dublin at the | Dead Zoo Lab | , a fascinating new home for the Natural History Museum’s most-loved specimens now on display. The Lab invites families to explore approx. 1,300 objects from entomology to marine life, mammals, birds, reptiles, and more, all free to visit (booking required only for groups). Highlights include delicate 19th-century Blaschka glass marine creatures, uprooted treasures like the dodo skeleton, an eel famously choking on a frog, the grand Spoticus the giraffe, and the iconic giant Irish deer, some of which haven’t been seen in decades. The smaller, hands-on space is perfect for curious kids and adults alike, offering rotating exhibits and innovative interpretations while the main Natural History Museum on Merrion Street undergoes a major refurbishment. It’s a brilliant way to keep the wonder of the Dead Zoo alive, without spending a cent.
Address: Collins Barracks, Benburb St, Stoneybatter, Dublin, D07 XKV4, Ireland

Title: MoCo Health Post-partum App
Description: Created by Eimear Lynch and Aoife Harvey, this innovative app offers women’s health physiotherapy support in a convenient, digital format. With over 20 years of combined experience, they offer 84 daily videos—think pelvic-floor reminders, strength-building sessions, and honest, no-taboo talk about everything from prolapse to postnatal hormones. Wrapped in clear, compassionate guidance, MoCo helps rebuild your body and confidence during the demanding fourth trimester. If the idea of doing pelvic-floor exercises while chasing a toddler makes you laugh—and cry—this app has got your back (and your core).

Title: MoLI – Museum of Literature Ireland
Description: MoLI – A Literary Adventure in the Heart of Dublin | Step into MoLI (Museum of Literature Ireland) at UCD Newman House on St. Stephen’s Green, a brilliant destination for families and anyone who loves stories. You’ll find children’s exhibitions and weekly programming that spark curiosity and encourage playful learning. | What makes MoLI especially wonderful for parents and kids is their | Learning Programme | . From family-friendly creative workshops and kid-centric exhibitions, to the LitLab, “ | Shut Your Eyes and See” | and | “MoLI in the Classroom” | for schools, there are so many ways for children and adults alike to explore Irish literature and find their own voice. If you’re curious, there are also learning resources, guided tours, podcasts, and an annual work experience programme for older students. | The LitLab | is a dedicated, family-friendly space that invites creativity, calm and discovery for visitors of all ages. Bright and welcoming, with comfy couches, views over the lush Iveagh Gardens, a trickling water fountain and a peaceful vibe, it’s a perfect spot for kids (and parents) to explore stories, draw, make, dream. Entry is included with your MoLI museum ticket (or free if you’re a MoLI member). | The Commons Cafe | is a hidden gem and super kid friendly, with a great kids menu and highchairs. MoLI is fully set up for family comfort with baby changing and easy access to the LitLab via a lift. A perfect spot for a rainy day or a peaceful afternoon, MoLI connects Dublin’s past and present one story at a time. | Step into the | Iveagh Gardens | after, through a secret door from the MoLI garden!
Address: 86 St Stephen's Green, Saint Kevin's, Dublin 2, D02 XY43, Ireland

Title: National Leprechaun Museum
Description: Step into a world where myths come alive, no magic wand required (though a twinkle in your eye helps)! | The National Leprechaun Museum | is Ireland’s first (and only!) immersive storytelling adventure dedicated to leprechauns and other enchanting creatures of our lore. As you wander through rooms that transform from cozy Irish dwellings to lush fairy hills and curious underground realms, each step is guided by a real-life storyteller, not dusty plaques. Expect optical-illusion tunnels, giant-scale furniture that flips your perspective (because feeling five inches tall is more fun than it sounds), and even a replica of the Giant’s Causeway to spark your imagination. | This isn’t child’s play, it’s a clever blend of whimsy and cultural pride, built for curious minds aged seven and up (and the young at heart). Title: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology
Description: FREE ADMISSION | The | National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology | on Kildare Street is a treasure trove for families and completely free to visit. Inside, you’ll find jaw-dropping highlights like the famous bog bodies (a little eerie, but older kids find them fascinating), glittering Celtic gold artefacts, and the Viking Ireland exhibition filled with swords, ships, and everyday objects that bring history to life. Attend a | Family Workshop | for free! There are also family trails, downloadable activity sheets, and regular workshops designed to make exploring interactive and fun. | For younger children, the bright mosaics in the entrance hall and the dramatic displays provide plenty to point at and wonder over, while older kids and teens can dive deeper into the stories of Ireland’s past. It’s one of those rare museums that entertains, educates, and sparks curiosity across all ageS.

Title: Rosemont After School

Title: Rotunda Hospital
Description: The Parental Education Classes at Rotunda Private offer a comprehensive and supportive preparation for expectant parents as they approach the birth of their baby. Delivered over five informative weeks, the course covers everything from maintaining physical and emotional well-being during pregnancy to understanding the stages of labour and birth, exploring pain relief options, and preparing for both breastfeeding and formula feeding. | Parents also gain practical skills in newborn care, safe sleep practices, postnatal recovery, and returning to everyday life with a new baby. Led by a team of expert midwives, physiotherapists, and healthcare professionals, the classes are held in a relaxed and welcoming environment, with Saturday sessions including lunch, free parking, and a guided tour of the Rotunda Hospital Labour Ward
Address: Parnell Square E, Rotunda, Dublin 1, D01 P5W9

Title: Rotunda Mental Health
Description: Rotunda Hospital – Specialist Perinatal Mental Health Support | At the celebrated Rotunda Hospital in Dublin, the Specialist Perinatal Mental Health Service offers expert care for women facing mental health challenges during pregnancy and up to one year after birth. While it operates strictly by referral (via GP, midwife, or other healthcare professionals) and appointments only, Rotunda also offers a range of practical support—like the “Me to Mum” antenatal and postnatal groups, birth reflection sessions for postpartum processing, breastfeeding workshops, and video-led wellbeing classes—to ensure parents feel informed, supported, and empowered throughout their early parenting journey
Address: The Rotunda Hospital, Parnell Square, Dublin 1,

Title: Royal Irish Academy of Music

Title: SENSEable Kids Events
Description: SENSEable Kids Events is a Dublin-based company specializing in sensory-rich entertainment for children, offering a variety of engaging activities tailored to different age groups and event types. Title: Sandycove Beach
Description: Sandycove Beach is a lovely small inlet with fine sand, made famous by the Martello Tower where the writer James Joyce once stayed for a week and now hosts a small Joycean museum, which is open in summer time. Sandycove beach is very popular with families, as the water to shallow enough to paddle and is perfect for picnics and bathing. But get there early to nab a good spot as it’s packed on a hot summers day. The beach also is home to the famous Forty Foot, where you’ll find brave swimmers having a dip all year round.

Title: Sandymount Art
Description: Sandymount School of Art is unique in Dublin in the approach to creativity. Every child is expertly coached and tutored and produces unique work. Creativity is supported and encouraged | Sandymount School of Art’s approach will support the development of every child’s character and individuality.

Title: Sandymount Strand
Description: Stretching along the Strand Road, the Promenade is a popular walking place and with outstanding views over Sandymount Strand to Poolbeg, Irishtown Nature Park and Dun Laoghaire. | It’s perfect for a stroll when the tide is out, while collecting seashells with the little ones or picnics during the summer months. There are better beaches for swimming but it’s perfect for paddling.

Title: Sarah, Parent and Matrescence Coach & Educator
Description: Sarah, Parent and Matrescence Coach brings over 15 years of teaching experience and a deeply compassionate understanding of modern motherhood to her work. She specialises in helping parents navigate the emotional shifts of matrescence—the profound transformation into motherhood—blending neuroscience, child development, and inner work to guide you toward calmer, more connected parenting (and less perfectionism). Whether you’re feeling overwhelmed, disconnected from yourself, or unsure about managing big emotions (both yours and your child’s), she offers a judgment-free space to rediscover your strength, clarity, and confidence—so you can parent with presence and purpose

Title: Scrummy Mummy Cakes
Description: Treat every occasion like the celebration it deserves with Scrummy Mummy Cakes’ gorgeous, custom-made creations—from elegant wedding cakes to playful novelty designs. Title: Sculpted by Aimee

Title: Sean Moore Park Playground
Description: Sean Moore Park Playground in Sandymount is a vibrant, sea-themed play area that offers a delightful outdoor experience for families. Designed with children of all ages in mind, the playground features a variety of equipment, including a lighthouse climbing frame, zip wire, monkey bars, trampoline, swings, musical toys, tunnels, and hills. | The park’s coastal location provides beautiful views near the beach, making it an ideal spot for picnics and outdoor activities. Title: Senco Sensory Solutions
Description: Planning a birthday or special get-together for a child who thrives in a sensory-friendly environment? Title: Seoidín

Title: Sharp Kids
Description: Sharp Kids classes are a fun and lively introduction to music, in preparation for the learning of the piano and other musical instruments. Suitable for 3 to 6 year olds, this training will begin to develop beat, rhythm, pitch and aural awareness, laying good foundations for the future.

Title: Silly Billy Parties
Description: Silly Billy Parties is renowned for delivering high-energy, interactive birthday parties that captivate children aged 1 to 14. Led by Ronan MacGabhann, a seasoned performer with over 20 years of experience, Silly Billy Parties offers a variety of themed shows, including Magic & Ventriloquism, Princess, Pirate Adventure, and Superhero parties. Title: Sinead Kelly Coaching

Title: Sinéad Feeney Photography

Title: Skerries Sailing Club

Title: Sleepease

Title: Slugs & Snails

Address: The Crescent, Termon, County Roscommon, Ireland

Title: Solas Coaching
Description: Solas Coaching, founded by Orla Donoghue—a single parent herself—is dedicated to empowering single parents, co-parents, and solo parents to reclaim confidence, cultivate balance, and create a life they can truly be proud of. Offering tailored 1:1 coaching programmes online (and in London), Solas provides a safe, flexible, and empathetic space to overcome overwhelm, guilt, or isolation through personalised support and mindset shifts that lead to lasting positive change.

Title: Sole

Title: Sonny Bear

Title: St Stephen’s Green

Title: St. Anne's Park

Title: The Irish National War Memorial Gardens
Description: FREE ADMISSION | The Irish National War Memorial Gardens | in Islandbridge offer a tranquil outdoor experience for families seeking a blend of nature, history, and reflection. Title: The Jeanie Johnston
